The noun is from Middle English swolow, swolwe, from Old English swelh, swelg (“gulf, chasm”) and ġeswelge (“gulf, chasm, abyss, whirlpool”), both from Proto-West Germanic *swelg, *swalgi, from Proto-Germanic *swelgaz, *swalgiz. Cognate with Old English swiliġe (“pit”), Scots swelch, swellie, swallie (“an abyss in the sea, whirpool”), Middle Low German swelch (“whirlpool, eddy”), Dutch zwelg (“gorge, chasm, gullet, throat”), Old Norse svelgr (“whirlpool, current, stream”).

senses.definition: To move food, drink, or saliva from your mouth down into your stomach.

examples.en: Chew your food well before you swallow it.
examples.vi: Hãy nhai kỹ thức ăn trước khi nuốt.

examples.en: He swallowed hard because he was nervous.
examples.vi: Anh ấy nuốt nước bọt vì quá hồi hộp.

senses.definition: To accept an unlikely story, excuse, or idea without questioning it.

examples.en: Did she really swallow that ridiculous excuse?
examples.vi: Cô ấy thật sự tin lời biện cớ nực cười đó sao?

senses.definition: To hold back your feelings, or accept an unpleasant remark or situation.

examples.en: He had to swallow his pride and apologize to his boss.
examples.vi: Anh ấy phải dẹp bỏ lòng tự ái và xin lỗi sếp.

examples.en: She swallowed her anger and remained completely silent.
examples.vi: Cô ấy kìm nén cơn giận và hoàn toàn im lặng.

senses.definition: To cover, enclose, or absorb something completely so that it disappears.

examples.en: The dark waves swallowed the tiny wooden boat.
examples.vi: Những con sóng đen ngòm đã nuốt chửng chiếc thuyền gỗ nhỏ.

thesaurus.definition: pass through the esophagus as part of eating or drinking
engulf and destroy
enclose or envelop completely, as if by swallowing
utter unclearly

wiktionary.gloss: To cause (food, drink etc.) to pass from the mouth into the stomach; to take into the stomach through the throat.
To take (something) in so that it disappears; to consume, absorb.

examples: My throat was so sore that I was unable to swallow.
wiktionary.gloss: To take food down into the stomach; to make the muscular contractions of the oesophagus to achieve this, often taken as a sign of nervousness or strong emotion.
To accept easily or without questions; to believe, accept.
To engross; to appropriate; usually with up.

examples: to swallow one's opinions
wiktionary.gloss: To retract; to recant.

examples: to swallow an affront or insult
wiktionary.gloss: To put up with; to bear patiently or without retaliation.
To swallow semen after oral sex, as opposed to spitting it out.

senses.definition: A small migratory bird with pointed wings and a forked tail that feeds on flying insects.

examples.en: Swallows return to our village every spring.
examples.vi: Những đàn chim én trở về làng chúng tôi vào mỗi mùa xuân.

senses.definition: An act of swallowing, or the small amount of liquid swallowed at one time.

examples.en: He took a quick swallow of water before speaking.
examples.vi: Anh ấy uống nhanh một ngụm nước trước khi nói.

thesaurus.definition: a small amount of liquid food
the act of swallowing
small long-winged songbird noted for swift graceful flight and the regularity of its migrations

examples: He took the aspirin with a single swallow of water.

The opening in a pulley block between the sheave and shell through which the rope passes.
Any of various carbohydrate-based dishes that are swallowed without much chewing, commonly paired and eaten with various types of soup.
A small, migratory bird of the Hirundinidae family with long, pointed, moon-shaped wings and a forked tail which feeds on the wing by catching insects.
